items.title: USN-9003-1: Linux kernel (NVIDIA) vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that some AMD processors did not properly perform Reverse Map Table (RMP) checks when the IOMMU accessed certain host buffers. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory.

items.title: USN-9002-1: Linux kernel (NVIDIA Tegra) vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that the io_uring subsystem in the Linux kernel did not properly handle canceled task work when processing certain wait operations, leading to the operation being performed in the wrong task context. items.title: USN-9001-1: ca-certificates update
items.summary: It was discovered that the ca-certificates JKS integration was not working properly, resulting in CA certificates removed from the system bundle not being removed from the JKS keystore. This update corrects the feature and resyncs the keystore with the system CA certificates list.

items.title: USN-8955-2: nginx vulnerabilities
items.summary: USN-8955-1 fixed vulnerabilities in nginx in Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. items.title: USN-7230-3: FRR regression
items.summary: USN-7230-2 fixed vulnerabilities in FRR. Unfortunately, the fix for CVE-2024-55553 introduced a regression in RPKI support, causing FRR to stop processing RPKI updates after the first one, so routes were not revalidated when RPKI data changed. In Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, the BGP daemon also failed to start

items.title: USN-8972-2: HAProxy regression
items.summary: USN-8972-1 fixed vulnerabilities in HAProxy. On Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, the update caused a regression when processing certain chunked requests. This update fixes the problem. We apologize for the inconvenience. Original advisory details: It was discovered that HAProxy incorrectly handled truncated HTTP/2

items.title: USN-9000-1: Twisted vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Twisted's IMAP server mishandled wildcard patterns in mailbox list commands. An authenticated remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Twisted to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service.
